propositions: Fixed-count compaction cadence (threshold=10) produces superlinear Θ(N²) retained-snapshot bytes because every ~T events writes a complete full-state snapshot and retains all prior snapshots append-only without deletion.

Geometric and byte/replay-cost-aware cadence policies achieve Θ(N) retained-snapshot bytes and Θ(log N) snapshot count on the identical workload, with byte-cost bounding replayed bytes to α times the active snapshot size.

All three cadence candidates preserve ADR 0035 contracts (conservative fold horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, mixed-version rollback, two-clone convergence) because they change only the WHEN trigger predicate, not snapshot placement, source_event_uuids, retire/restore rules, or replay ordering.

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence with configurable alpha reduces retired-snapshot bytes 344× (N=8,000 events, α=1.0) compared to fixed-count control while keeping read cost bounded to a small multiple of unavoidable snapshot load.
Production implementation of byte/replay-cost-aware cadence requires an ADR and decomposition into independently reviewable tasks; no implementation begins in this research ticket.
